why: A username belongs to a real name exactly when it is a permutation of it, so each name maps to an anagram key (sorted letters or a 26-letter count). Count keys over allNames in a hash map; a real name is recurring when its key has count >= 2.
hints: Two usernames belong to the same person if and only if they are anagrams. What canonical form do all anagrams share?
Map every string to its sorted letters. Count how often each key appears in allNames, then look each real name's key up in that count.
One Counter over allNames (names are at most 10 letters, so sorting each is cheap), filter realNames with count >= 2, sort the result. Overall O((n + m) L log L + n log n).
pitfalls: Return ["None"] (a list with the string None) when nobody qualifies, not an empty list.
The real name itself may or may not appear in allNames; count permutations including the exact spelling.
The output must be in lexicographic order, not input order.
